title: Run 30 to 200 CISOs — your call
summary: Panel size is a dial: 30 for a fast read, up to 200 for a tighter one. The floor of 30 keeps every answer statistically honest.
body: Choose your N. A smaller panel is faster and cheaper; a larger one narrows the confidence band. Below 30 the product refuses — that's the line where the statistics stop being meaningful.

title: Introducing the Príncipe news center
summary: Product updates now reach you in two places: in-app, and here on the site.
body:
We're adding a single place to follow what's changing in Príncipe — feature updates, calibration improvements, security and release notes.

One source, two channels: every update appears **in the app** (delivered through the same signed knowledge feed that updates your panel) and **here on the site**. You'll see what's new without hunting through release notes.

title: Watch a question become a decision
summary: A two-minute run, recorded live against a self-hosted instance.
body: See a real security question go in and a calibrated decision come out — stance, the segments that split, the objections that block it, and an honest read on confidence.

title: Sharper verdicts — stance now reflects the full split
summary: A verdict can no longer read 'strong no' when only a small minority objects. Neutrality isn't opposition.
body:
The decision stance now derives from the **balance** between support and opposition, not support alone. A *Strong* verdict requires a clear majority *and* a wide net margin; abstentions and neutrals no longer count as 'against'.

So if only 8% of the panel objects, you'll never see a 'strong no'. Existing reports were backfilled, and the on-screen summary and the PDF export now always agree with the buy-rate.

title: New write-up: Príncipe vs naive N-shot
summary: Is the panel real signal, or the same prompt sampled 100 times? A controlled experiment against 9,600+ real CISO responses.
body: Three conditions on 10 benchmark questions. Full Príncipe missed by 14pp; naive N-shot by 35pp — a 21-point gap the null hypothesis can't explain.

title: Panel recalibrated — mean error 47 → 18 points
summary: A panel-layer fix plus type-aware calibration cut the gap to real CISO opinion by more than half.
body:
We measured the panel against real CISO surveys and closed the gap step by step — overall mean error fell from **47 to 18 points**.

The biggest lever was panel heterogeneity: personas now carry a business-pragmatist disposition alongside the security-purist one, so the room *splits* where real CISOs split instead of collapsing to 0% or 100%. Where a question type still isn't calibrated, the answer comes back marked *directional* — honest about its own confidence.

title: Self-host in one command
summary: One line installs Docker if needed, clones the repo, and boots the whole stack.
body: A first-run wizard takes your API key and brings up Postgres, the Bayesian statistician, and the web app. Pick your OS on the download page and paste a single command.
